function: Infers the full high-dimensional beamforming matrix of the base station from a low-dimensional channel and beamforming matrix, avoiding full channel estimation and WMMSE iterations (p. 2).
system: Downlink mmWave, BS with 32 antennas (64 in Fig. 8), 4 single-antenna users, full-digital beamforming, 60 GHz, 50 MHz, spacing 0.5 or 0.1 wavelength; no RIS (p. 4).
method: Conditional WGAN-GP: encoder-decoder generator with skip connections and convolutional discriminator, trained offline in a supervised way on WMMSE beamforming targets with Wasserstein-GP plus L2 loss (p. 3).
data_channel: WAIR-D scenario 2 (open-source dataset from practical scenario maps, one BS); 250 random samples split 4:1 for training and testing; 5 paths; estimation error -20 dB (p. 4).
test_conditions: Same WAIR-D map for training and testing (4:1 split); SNR 10 dB, estimation error -20 dB; antenna spacing 0.5 or 0.1 wavelength and low-dimensional antenna count varied (p. 4).
baselines: Classical: WMMSE (spectral efficiency, running time). Learned: DNN of [13] (self-supervised hybrid deep learning beamforming, F. Zhu et al., EUSIPCO 2023), compared in spectral efficiency (p. 5).
metrics: NMSE of the beamforming matrix (dB, over iterations), system sum spectral efficiency (bit/s/Hz), running time (ms) (p. 4-5).
complexity: Big-O given: WMMSE O(L(Nt_high)^3) versus proposed O(L(Nt_low)^3)+O(Nr(Nt_high)^2+(Nt_high)^3); runtime over 50% lower than WMMSE in Fig. 6 (p. 4).
openness: No code released; uses the public open-source WAIR-D dataset (https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.02159, ref. [14]) (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "recently released open-source dataset WAIR-D [14]". Trained and tested on WAIR-D scenario 2 (p. 4), a public dataset built on real maps, not 3GPP or DeepMIMO; reviewer to confirm.
q2_support: p. 4: "randomly select 250 samples from the dataset and split them into two subsets with a 4:1 ratio". Test data is a held-out part of the same data; no new scenario or configuration; transfer learning only mentioned as possible (p. 3).
q3_support: p. 5: "the proposed method and the WMMSE as well as the DNN [13] method". Fig. 8 compares spectral efficiency with WMMSE (non-learned) and with the earlier learned DNN beamformer of [13].
q4_support: p. 4: "the complexity of the original WMMSE algorithm and the proposed algorithm could be expressed as" O(L(Nt_high)^3) and O(L(Nt_low)^3)+O(Nr(Nt_high)^2+(Nt_high)^3); runtime in Fig. 6.
q5_support: p. 4: "recently released open-source dataset WAIR-D [14]". Trains and tests on this public dataset (link in ref. [14], p. 5); the paper releases no code of its own.
notes: Preprint arXiv:2405.00391v2 of LWC letter 'Beamforming Inferring by Conditional WGAN-GP for Holographic Antenna Arrays'.
